assessments.explanation: The claim states criticism is 'frequently' directed toward short hours for breakfast. The word 'frequently' requires at least three distinct cited tweets supporting this specific criticism. Only one tweet (E026) explicitly criticizes the short hours for breakfast, stating it ends at 10:30 weekdays and 11:00 weekends. Another tweet (E002) mentions not wanting McDonald's to serve all day but concedes until noon, which does not constitute criticism of the short hours themselves. The other cited tweets address unrelated topics like sauce packets, food quality, location, or general dissatisfaction. Since only one distinct tweet supports the specific detail of 'short hours for breakfast', the claim fails to meet the threshold for 'frequently'.

assessments.explanation: The claim states criticism is 'frequently' directed toward short hours for breakfast. The word 'frequently' requires at least three distinct cited tweets supporting this specific criticism. Only one tweet (E026) explicitly criticizes the short hours for breakfast, stating it ends at 10:30 weekdays and 11:00 weekends. Another tweet (E002) mentions not wanting McDonald's to serve all day but concedes until noon, which does not constitute criticism of the short hours themselves. The other cited tweets address unrelated topics like sauce packets, food quality, location, or general dissatisfaction. Since only one distinct tweet supports the specific detail of 'short hours for breakfast', the claim fails to meet the threshold for 'frequently'.
